subject: Clarification on usage commit reconciliation and credit mechanics (Acme AI)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>

Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@acme.ai>, contracts@acme.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on commit reconciliation cadence and make-good handling

Jordan — thanks for the term sheet. We're close on internal approval but Procurement has two follow-ups before we can sign:

1) Reconciliation cadence: can you confirm whether true-ups are done quarterly or annually by default? The term sheet references an annual reconciliation but our legal wants a quarterly option for larger commits.

2) Make-goods vs credits: in cases where actual usage < committed minimum, does Redwood provide a make-good (one-time credit) or automatic carry-forward to the next quarter? How do you handle partial quarters if we ramp mid-term?

3) Overage pricing: if we exceed the committed tiers, what's the overage per-token rate and is it pro-rated for partial months?

We flagged these because our finance needs the invoicing model documented for our SOW. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships | Acme AI
From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
To: laura.chen@acme.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on commit reconciliation cadence and make-good handling

Laura — great questions, thanks. High level answers below; I included Marissa (sales lead) and Vivek (billing/ops) for the details we’ll probably want in the SOW. TL;DR: we support quarterly or annual true-ups; make-goods are available as credits or one-time refunds depending on contract language and timing.

Summary:
- Reconciliation cadence: default is annual but quarterly true-ups are supported for commitments >= $200k ARR or at your request.
- Make-goods vs credits: we offer an account-level credit (applied to the next invoice) by default. For enterprise requests we can structure a one-time cash make-good; that requires exec approval.
- Overage pricing: overage is priced at the next lower discount tier rate (i.e., you pay the non-committed per-token rate for excess) and is billed monthly, pro-rated to the day.

I'll defer to Marissa/Vivek for exact mechanics and a worked example. If useful, we can propose quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months while you ramp.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question on commit reconciliation cadence and make-good handling

Hi Laura — adding a few specifics you can include in your SOW. I'm attaching the term sheet v7 and a sample Q3 schedule. Key points:

- Quarterly true-up option: if you elect quarterly true-ups we reconcile actual usage against committed tokens at the end of each quarter. If usage < committed we apply a credit equal to the difference (committed - actual) at the committed unit price. Credits are issued on the following month's invoice.

- Annual true-up: reconciliation against the full 12-month committed amount. If short, credits are issued on the first invoice after year-end reconciliation.

- Make-good (cash) requests: for credits to be converted to a cash make-good we require sign-off from Sales Director + Finance; this is generally granted for churn-sensitive renewal scenarios or material procurement requirements.

- Mid-term ramp and partial quarters: commits are measured on a monthly token-equivalent basis. If you ramp mid-quarter we prorate the committed amount for that quarter (days in service / days in quarter * committed monthly tokens). Example: if a 9/1 start for a quarterly commit, we prorate August to 2/30 days, etc. (Vivek, please correct if I misstated the proration calc).

- Overage math: Overage rate = list per-token price for the tier above your commit threshold (so it’s the non-discounted incremental rate). Overage is billed on the monthly invoice with daily pro-ration if the burst crosses month boundaries.

Next steps: if that's acceptable I'll update the term sheet to add a clause for quarterly reconciliation and the proration formula, and include language for cash make-goods requiring exec approval.

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on commit reconciliation cadence and make-good handling

Laura — a couple of operational clarifications from billing/ops side:

1) Tokens and measurement window: we report token usage per calendar month (UTC). For reconciliation we aggregate months into quarter/year depending on selected cadence.

2) Rounding & thresholds: we round token counts to the nearest whole token for billing. We have a 1% floor tolerance for variance on large commits (>= 1B tokens) to avoid repeated micro-credits.

3) Credit application mechanics: credits from shortfalls are posted to your account as negative line items and will be visible on the next invoice. Credits can be auto-applied or held as an account credit that you can request to convert to a one-time refund (cash) with approval.

4) Audit & transparency: we'll provide a monthly usage CSV (stubbed link attached in the term sheet) and an online usage dashboard with token-level granularity.

Worked example (quarterly true-up):
- Committed Q3: 300M tokens at $0.0006/token (50% discount off list)
- Actual Q3 usage: 270M tokens
- Shortfall: 30M tokens -> credit = 30M * $0.0006 = $18,000 applied to October invoice

If you prefer annual true-up, the same math applies at year-end.

Happy to walk through a sample invoice with your finance team.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Billing & Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
